description: Organisational-alignment diagnostic. Effectiveness depends on seven interdependent elements being mutually consistent; misalignment between any two is a root-cause candidate for performance gaps.
best_for: Assessing readiness for a strategic shift or reorganisation
Explaining why a prior change initiative under-delivered

dimensions.name: Strategy
dimensions.description: The plan to build and sustain competitive advantage.
diagnostic_questions: Is the strategy explicit, and can middle management restate it?
Which KPIs prove the strategy is being executed?
Where does daily decision-making contradict the stated strategy?

dimensions.name: Structure
dimensions.description: Reporting lines, spans of control and how units are grouped.
diagnostic_questions: Where do decisions wait for escalation more than one level?
Which processes cross more than three organisational boundaries?

dimensions.name: Systems
dimensions.description: Formal procedures, workflows, controls and information flows (described as AS-IS context, not solutioned).
diagnostic_questions: Which controls exist on paper but are bypassed in practice?
Where is the same data re-keyed or reconciled manually?
Which management reports are produced but not used for decisions?

dimensions.name: Shared Values
dimensions.description: The core beliefs and norms that actually guide behaviour.
diagnostic_questions: What behaviour gets rewarded informally that contradicts stated values?
How do people describe 'how things really work here'?

dimensions.name: Style
dimensions.description: Leadership behaviour and the dominant management approach.
diagnostic_questions: Are decisions made by consensus, by decree, or by default?
How is bad news received by the leadership team?

dimensions.name: Staff
diagnostic_questions: Where are single points of failure in critical roles?
Which capabilities are outsourced that should be core, or vice versa?

dimensions.name: Skills
dimensions.description: Distinctive competences of the organisation as a whole.
diagnostic_questions: Which capabilities do customers actually pay for?
Which skills will the target operating model require that do not exist today?

pitfalls: Treating the seven elements as a checklist instead of testing pairwise alignment
Reporting Systems as software inventory rather than as procedures and information flows
Skipping the soft elements (Shared Values, Style, Staff, Skills) because they are harder to evidence
sources: Waterman, Peters, Phillips — 'Structure Is Not Organization', Business Horizons (1980)
